content_voiceover: This slide outlines the standard hemostasis workup. It always starts with a personal and family bleeding history plus physical exam, marked here with double asterisks because a good history is actually the single most sensitive screening tool, more so than any individual lab test. From there, first-level testing splits into two arms. The platelet arm includes the platelet count from a routine CBC, plus platelet function tests, specifically the PFA-100 closure time and formal platelet aggregometry, which assess how well platelets adhere and aggregate rather than just how many there are. The plasmatic coagulation arm covers the classic trio, PT, aPTT, and thrombin time, which interrogate the extrinsic, intrinsic, and common pathways respectively. For boards, remember the pattern-recognition logic, isolated platelet-type bleeding, mucocutaneous, petechiae, points you toward the platelet arm, while deep bleeding into joints or muscles points you toward the coagulation factor arm.
keypoints: Bleeding history + physical exam = most sensitive first screen
Coagulation factors: PT, aPTT, thrombin time
Mucocutaneous bleeding → platelet workup; deep bleeding → factor workup
keypoint_voiceover: Keep two tracks in mind. Platelet studies, count plus function testing with PFA-100 or aggregometry, evaluate primary hemostasis. Coagulation studies, PT, aPTT, and thrombin time, evaluate secondary hemostasis. And never skip the bleeding history and exam, it's the highest-yield screening step of all and guides which track to pursue first.
